item.title: Core Concepts
item.description:
The parts of Joulie and the control loop that ties them together. Read it before the Quickstart.

What Joulie is

Joulie is a Kubernetes-native energy management system that keeps a digital twin of every managed node. The twin is fed by telemetry: CPU and GPU power read from Prometheus as the OpenTelemetry hardware metrics hw.energy and hw.power or as Kepler energy counters, and per-pod utilization from cAdvisor. It drives two outcomes: power caps and governor presets that the node agent enforces (RAPL, NVML), and scheduling, where the scheduler extender steers new pods toward the nodes with the best energy and performance trade-off.

item.title: Quickstart
item.description:
Install Joulie on a cluster and check that it manages your nodes. New to Joulie? Read Core Concepts first, or try it with only Docker in the Tutorials.

Prerequisites

  • Kubernetes with Node Feature Discovery (NFD) deployed.
  • Prometheus at http://prometheus-operated.monitoring:9090 with its OTLP receiver on (--web.enable-otlp-receiver), receiving hw.energy or hw.power for each node. values/prometheus-grafana.yaml configures kube-prometheus-stack this way (Prometheus settings), and examples/04-otel-collector-bridge converts Kepler, dcgm-exporter and AMD device-metrics-exporter metrics into those names.
  • Without that data every node reads 0 W (source prometheus-no-data). To run without Prometheus, set controllerManager.env.NODE_POWER_SOURCE=static.
  • Optional, for real enforcement: writable RAPL power limit files or cpufreq sysfs on the nodes, and NVML for NVIDIA GPUs.

Install

helm upgrade --install joulie oci://registry.cern.ch/joulie/joulie \
 --version <version> \
 -n joulie-system \
 --create-namespace \
 -f values/joulie.yaml

Upgrading an existing release? helm upgrade never updates CRDs: apply the new ones first, as Upgrading shows.

item.title: Tutorials
item.description:
Six tutorials take you from a first install to the main features, each a directory under examples/ with a README to follow. The first three run on the simulated cluster, the real Joulie components managing ten emulated bare-metal nodes in one Docker container, so start there even before a real install.

Tutorial What you will see Needs
01 Simulated cluster A first install; the hardware the agent discovers (NodeHardware); the digital twin (NodeTwin); power profiles turned into RAPL and GPU caps, down to the files the agent writes; capping a node by hand; kubectl joulie on a live workload Docker, Go, kubectl, helm, jq
02 Workload classes Performance and standard pods; the scheduler extender keeping performance pods off eco nodes, and the scores behind each placement the cluster of 01
03 Grafana dashboard kube-prometheus-stack scraping Joulie, and the dashboard the chart ships the cluster of 01, or yours
04 OpenTelemetry Collector bridge Kepler, dcgm-exporter and the AMD device-metrics-exporter turned into the hw.* metrics the digital twin reads Docker
05 Governor presets CPU and GPU governor presets, a second energy dimension next to the caps, on six hardware families Docker, Go, kubectl, helm, jq
06 Cooling and PUE Cooling models and the PUE they give for a power trace, with a Modelica FMU Python, Docker

Then install Joulie on your cluster with the Quickstart. The experiments run Joulie at scale on the simulator.

item.title: Pod Compatibility for Joulie
item.description:
How to tell Joulie where a pod may run. A single pod annotation expresses its placement intent:

joulie.io/workload-class: performance | standard

The scheduler extender reads this annotation and steers pods accordingly. No node affinity rules are needed.

The controller manager labels each managed node joulie.io/power-profile (performance or eco) with its current power state. You do not need to use that label for placement: the annotation is the single source of truth for placement intent.

item.title: Agent Runtime Modes
item.description:
How the chart deploys the node agent. Pick the mode with agent.mode:

agent.mode Pods Use
daemonset (default) one pod per managed node (charts/joulie/templates/agent-daemonset.yaml) real hardware
pool a StatefulSet whose pods each run many logical per-node agents (agent-statefulset.yaml) KWOK experiments over the simulator’s HTTP API
emulated one Deployment per node of the simulated cluster (agent-emulated.yaml), reading that node’s emulated /sys and GPU tools the simulated cluster
none no agent

DaemonSet mode (real hardware)

Use it on real nodes, where the agent writes the power limits under the host’s /sys. The chart sets:

item.title: CPU Support and Power Capping
item.description:
How Joulie caps the CPU packages of a node and sets their frequency governor, through NodeTwin intents the agent enforces.

Contract model

CPU intent is in NodeTwin.spec.cpu. The first field present wins:

  1. packagePowerCapWatts: an absolute cap.
  2. packagePowerCapPctOfMax: a percentage of the node’s cap range.

Policy behavior

Profile CPU cap CPU governor on a CPU-only node, when governor control is on
performance (or draining) high, often 100 % CPU_GOVERNOR_PERFORMANCE_PRESET, default performance
eco lower CPU_GOVERNOR_ECO_PRESET, default efficiency (provisional)

See Governor policy.

item.title: CRD and Policy Model
item.description:
The contract between Joulie’s components: pods state demand, node labels expose supply, NodeHardware publishes what a node is, and NodeTwin carries what it should be. Use this page to read or debug these objects.

APIs
Group and version joulie.io/v1alpha1
CRDs NodeHardware (nodehardwares), NodeTwin (nodetwins), both cluster-scoped
Definitions config/crd/bases/joulie.io_nodehardwares.yaml, config/crd/bases/joulie.io_nodetwins.yaml

Demand model (workloads)

Demand comes from the joulie.io/workload-class pod annotation:

  • performance: the pod carries joulie.io/workload-class: performance and is kept off eco and draining nodes.
  • standard (default): no annotation, or standard. It can run on any node; scoring steers it toward eco when performance nodes are congested.

Supply model (nodes)

Signal Values Set by
node label joulie.io/power-profile performance, eco controller manager
NodeTwin.status.schedulableClass performance, eco, draining controller manager (twin)

draining is the transition safeguard while a node moves toward eco with performance pods still on it; the scheduler extender filters it out for performance pods. schedulableClass is internal: users express placement intent only with the pod annotation.

item.title: GPU Support (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel)
item.description:
How Joulie caps the GPUs of a node and sets their clock governor on NVIDIA, AMD and Intel, through NodeTwin intents the agent enforces.

Validation status

GPU support has been validated in simulator mode only; the host code paths are written for bare-metal NVIDIA, AMD and Intel nodes, which have not run them yet.

Contract model

NodeTwin.spec.gpu.powerCap holds a per-GPU cap with scope: perGpu. The first field present wins:

  1. capWattsPerGpu: an absolute cap.
  2. capPctOfMax: a percentage of the per-GPU maximum.

The same cap applies to every GPU of the node.

item.title: Simulated Cluster
item.description:
The simulated cluster runs the real Joulie components on emulated bare-metal nodes, on one machine with Docker. The agent discovers and caps emulated hardware through the same files and tools it uses on a real node, the controller manager reads node power from Prometheus, and the scheduler extender scores real pods.

Use it to see a change to the agent, the controller manager, the extender, the chart or the simulator work across components. A change to discovery or capping alone is checked faster by the hwemu tests in cmd/agent (go test ./cmd/agent/ -run Hwemu).

item.title: Workload Scenarios
item.description: A workload scenario runs a workload through the simulated cluster and checks what happened: whether the jobs completed, where they were placed, how long they took, what energy they used, and how Joulie’s settings compare with each other or with no Joulie at all. The jobs are real Kubernetes Jobs on KWOK Nodes, driven by the simulator’s v1 engine on the emulated hardware, so a cap the agent writes slows the jobs on that Node.

item.title: Installation
item.description:
This page installs the simulator into a Kubernetes cluster you already have, or runs it from a workstation. To try Joulie with nothing but Docker, use the simulated cluster instead: it creates the cluster and installs everything.

The commands use the namespace joulie-sim-demo and the release joulie-simulator, the defaults of make simulator-install.

Prerequisites

  • A Kubernetes cluster (real, or kind for local work), with kubectl pointed at it.
  • helm v3 or later.

Install with Helm

helm upgrade --install joulie-simulator oci://registry.cern.ch/joulie/joulie-sim \
 --version <version> -n joulie-sim-demo --create-namespace

helm show values oci://registry.cern.ch/joulie/joulie-sim --version <version> prints the values you can override; helm uninstall joulie-simulator -n joulie-sim-demo removes it. The chart models the Nodes labelled joulie.io/managed=true (SIM_NODE_SELECTOR); KWOK and Standalone Modes says how to point Joulie at it.

item.title: Emulate Mode
item.description:
Emulate mode emulates the bare-metal nodes of a cluster spec at the boundary the agent sees: the files it reads and writes, and the GPU tools it runs. An unmodified agent then runs its real discovery and capping code against each node, while Kubernetes scheduling stays real. The simulated cluster runs it; to run it yourself, see Installation. Nodes the spec does not list keep the label-based model of KWOK and standalone modes.

Turn it on with SIM_EMULATE=true and SIM_CLUSTER_SPEC; every variable is under Simulator emulate mode.

item.title: KWOK and Standalone Modes
item.description:
Outside emulate mode the simulator models each node from its labels: it keeps per-node power, cap and thermal state in memory and serves it over HTTP, with no files and no GPU tools. It runs in one of two ways:

  • KWOK mode: a Kubernetes cluster whose worker nodes are KWOK fake nodes. The real controller manager, scheduler extender and agent in pool mode run against the simulator’s HTTP API. The benchmark experiments run this way.
  • Standalone mode (SIM_STANDALONE=true): no Kubernetes. The simulator places the jobs of a trace and runs the policy baselines itself, in simulated time.

How KWOK mode works

  1. Node labels give each fake node its simulated hardware.
  2. The controller manager resolves that hardware and writes the desired profile and caps into NodeTwin.spec.
  3. The agent (pool mode) reads NodeTwin.spec and sends control intents to /control/{node}.
  4. The simulator applies them, advances power, energy and job progress, and serves telemetry on /otlp/telemetry/{node}.
  5. The next reconcile reacts to the new state; the scheduler extender scores pods from NodeTwin.status.

Set it up:

item.title: Joulie Controller Manager
item.description:
The controller manager is Joulie’s cluster-level decision engine: it decides which nodes supply performance capacity and which can safely supply eco, and publishes that through Kubernetes objects and labels. It never writes host power interfaces; the agent does.

Responsibilities

Part Runs Does
Twin controller every RECONCILE_INTERVAL (1 min) reads measured power and NodeHardware, writes the twin’s scores to NodeTwin.status (Digital Twin)
Policy controller every RECONCILE_INTERVAL classifies demand, runs the policy, applies the downgrade guard, writes NodeTwin.spec (caps and, with governor control on, governor presets) and the joulie.io/power-profile label
Facility poller every FACILITY_POLL_INTERVAL (30 s), off by default reads ambient temperatures, IT, cooling and rack power, carbon intensity (Measured inputs)

The controller manager decides what each node should be; the agent decides how to apply it on the node.

item.title: Workload Generation
item.description:
workloadgen (simulator/cmd/workloadgen) writes synthetic traces of AI cluster workloads for the simulator to run. Workload Simulator says how the simulator runs them.

go run ./simulator/cmd/workloadgen --out trace.jsonl --jobs 200 --seed 7

The traces hold CPU and GPU jobs, memory-bound jobs, and workloads of several pods, such as distributed training and hyperparameter searches. Network, disk and framework communication are not modelled: their cost is folded into each workload’s utilisation and bottleneck signals.

Trace format

A trace is JSON Lines. A type=workload record is one logical workload with its pods by role, for inspection only; a type=job record is one runnable pod, and the simulator runs these.

item.title: Workload Simulator
item.description:
This page says how the simulator runs a workload trace: which Kubernetes objects it creates and how caps slow each job. Workload Generation describes the traces; Power Simulator the power side of a node.

Two engines: legacy and v1

SIM_WORKLOAD_MODEL selects the engine that runs a trace.

Engine Where Started by Kubernetes objects A job that cannot progress Results
legacy outside emulate mode SIM_WORKLOAD_TRACE_PATH, replayed from startup one bare pod per job, deleted when done completed by force after SIM_WORKLOAD_STALL_FORCE_COMPLETE (120 s) joulie_sim_job_* counters at /metrics
v1 emulate mode the run API, or SIM_WORKLOAD_TRACE_PATH as an implicit run one batch/v1 Job per group, completed through KWOK’s pod-complete Stage reported as stalled, never completed OTLP JSON Lines in the run directory, plus the run API’s status

v1 without emulate mode, and legacy with it, stop the start. The variables are in Simulator workloads and scenarios. Workload Scenarios run v1 workloads on the simulated cluster and check their completion, placement, slowdown and energy.

item.title: Power Simulator
item.description:
This page says how the simulator advances a modelled node (any node outside the emulate-mode cluster spec): its controls, its physics step and its telemetry. The models and their sources are in Hardware Modeling; how jobs progress is in Workload Simulator.

The physics step

A modelled node advances only in a physics step, in simulated time, never when it is read. One step moves caps, frequency, power and temperature toward their targets with their settling lags, in substeps of at most 100 ms, and integrates energy from the instantaneous power.

item.title: Hardware Calibration
item.description:
hwcalib (simulator/cmd/hwcalib) fits the physics of a hardware profile to a sweep measured on one of your nodes, so the simulator draws what your machine draws instead of the builtin profiles’ vendor figures and placeholders. hwcalib sweep records the sweep on the node; hwcalib fit writes the result as a local profile the simulator loads from SIM_PROFILES_DIR.

Recording a sweep

A sweep holds the node at a series of setpoints and records, at every sample, the node’s readings and the setpoints it held. Each setpoint needs at least 5 samples after it settles: with a 2 s sample period, 22 s or more.

item.title: Simulator Metrics
item.description:
This page lists every metric and event the simulator emits, to write a query or a dashboard against it. There are three kinds:

Kind Where Mode
Prometheus metrics about the simulator itself (joulie_sim_*) scraped at /metrics every mode
OpenTelemetry metrics and events about the emulated nodes and the facility metrics pushed as OTLP JSON over HTTP; events in events.jsonl, pushed when a logs endpoint is set emulate mode
Compatibility exporters: the Prometheus formats of Kepler, dcgm-exporter and the ROCm device-metrics-exporter /exporters/<name>/metrics, opt-in emulate mode

The OpenTelemetry names are spelled once, in pkg/otel/semconv, and the controller manager reads the same names back from Prometheus. Their Prometheus spelling is computed by pkg/otel/promname.

item.title: Hardware Modeling and Physical Power Model
item.description:
This page says what Joulie models about CPUs and GPUs and where the numbers come from. The agent uses these facts to resolve caps; the simulator uses them to turn utilization and controls into power and slowdown.

In the simulator these models are a test bed for Joulie’s behaviour, not evidence of energy savings: they rest on vendor figures, public measurements and assumptions. What meaningful experiments need is tracked in the milestone Evidence-based evaluation.

item.title: Joulie Agent
item.description:
The agent is Joulie’s node-side component: it discovers the node’s hardware and applies the caps and governor presets the controller manager plans. It does not plan policy.

Responsibilities

Every reconcile (RECONCILE_INTERVAL, 20 s), for each node it owns, the agent:

Step What
1 discovers CPU and GPU hardware, cap ranges and governors
2 publishes them as NodeHardware
3 reads the desired state in NodeTwin.spec
4 applies the governor presets and the CPU and GPU caps, through host interfaces or HTTP
5 reports the outcome in NodeTwin.status.controlStatus and on /metrics

Inputs and outputs

Inputs Outputs
NodeTwin.spec: profile, caps, governor presets NodeHardware: discovered hardware and capabilities
backend variables (TELEMETRY_CPU_SOURCE, TELEMETRY_CPU_CONTROL, TELEMETRY_GPU_CONTROL; default host) writes to RAPL, cpufreq and GPU interfaces, or the simulator over HTTP
node labels (hardware identity, NFD and GPU feature discovery) NodeTwin.status.controlStatus: applied, blocked, error or none per component
Prometheus metrics on /metrics (Metrics Reference)

NodeHardware is the agent’s output; you do not write it.

item.title: Digital Twin
item.description:
The digital twin turns each node’s measured power and hardware limits into a few scores the scheduler and the policy use. It is a closed-form model in the controller manager (pkg/controller/twin), computed every reconcile, and its output is NodeTwin.status.

What the digital twin computes

Field in NodeTwin.status Meaning Range Read by
predictedPowerHeadroomScore share of the node’s capped power budget still unused up to 100, negative when over budget scheduler (fallback)
predictedCoolingStressScore measured power over node TDP, scaled up in warm ambient air 0 to 100 scheduler
predictedPsuStressScore rack (or cluster) power over a 50 kW reference capacity 0 to 100 nobody yet
estimatedPUE cooling stress restated on a PUE scale 1.05 to 1.40 nobody yet
schedulableClass performance, eco or draining scheduler, controller manager
powerMeasurement measured power, TDP, capped budget and trend, per node watts scheduler
conditions AgentReporting: whether an agent enforces the caps the Agent column of kubectl get nodetwins

Every power score starts from the measured node power powerMeasurement.measuredNodePowerW, not from the caps.

item.title: Policy Algorithms
item.description:
A policy decides how many managed nodes run the performance profile; every other node runs eco. Pick one with POLICY_TYPE on the controller manager. The policies are in pkg/controller/policy/.

Demand is the number of pods annotated joulie.io/workload-class: performance; pods without the annotation are standard.

Which performance nodes

static_partition and queue_aware_v1 compute a count; the controller manager then splits it across hardware families (gpu:<model>, cpu:<model>) in proportion to family size, at least one node per family, keeping nodes already in performance first. A change of one in the count moves exactly one node. The split is exported as joulie_policy_family_nodes{family} and joulie_policy_family_performance_nodes{family}.

item.title: Scheduler Extender
item.description:
Joulie’s scheduler extender keeps performance pods off eco nodes and ranks the remaining nodes by power headroom and cooling stress. It is an HTTP extender that kube-scheduler calls; it does not replace kube-scheduler. The chart always deploys it; without it pods get standard Kubernetes scheduling.

How a pod gets scheduled (end-to-end)

  1. kube-scheduler picks up the new pod and runs its own filters (resources, taints, affinity).
  2. It calls Joulie’s POST /filter: performance pods lose the eco and draining nodes.
  3. It calls POST /prioritize: Joulie scores each remaining node 0 to 100 for this pod and returns it as a 0 to 10 priority.
  4. kube-scheduler adds Joulie’s priority, times the extender weight, to its own plugin scores and binds the pod to the best node.

Placement intent comes from one pod annotation, joulie.io/workload-class, so users write no scheduling rules. The extender does not migrate or evict pods and never overrides resource fits.

item.title: Energy-Aware Scheduling
item.description:
This page follows one placement decision from the hardware counters to the chosen node. Each stage is a separate component that hands its result to the next through Prometheus or a CRD, and each links to the page that documents it.

End-to-end pipeline

RAPL/NVML readings as OpenTelemetry metrics (or Kepler)
 -> Prometheus (OTLP receiver, or scrape)
 -> Digital twin (NodeTwin.status)
 -> Scheduler extender (filter + score)
 -> Placement decision

Stage 1: Telemetry collection

CPU (RAPL) and GPU (NVML, ROCm SMI) power reach Prometheus as the OpenTelemetry metrics hw.energy and hw.power, or through Kepler: Input metrics (OpenTelemetry).

item.title: Configuration Reference
item.description:
Complete reference for all Joulie environment variables. These are set via Helm values or directly in the Deployment/DaemonSet manifests.

Defaults listed below are the code defaults. The Helm chart (charts/joulie/values.yaml) overrides some of them: notably, the controller manager NODE_SELECTOR defaults to joulie.io/managed=true in the chart even though the code default is node-role.kubernetes.io/worker.

Booleans. The agent, the controller manager and the simulator read every on/off variable the same way: true, 1, yes or on, and false, 0, no or off, in any case, with surrounding spaces ignored. Unset or empty means the default. Any other value keeps the default and logs one warning naming the variable, so a typo never flips a switch. The exceptions are SIM_OTEL_FILE_METRICS, OTEL_SDK_DISABLED and fakesmi’s HWEMU_UNPRIVILEGED, whose rows say how they are read.

item.title: Input Telemetry and Actuation Interfaces
item.description:
How Joulie reads power and facility telemetry, and how the agent sends its control intents. Use it to wire Prometheus, an OpenTelemetry producer or the simulator to Joulie. Exported /metrics are on the Metrics Reference; the CRD fields are on CRD and Policy Model.

Backends

The same control logic runs on real hardware and on simulator or KWOK clusters; environment variables on the agent choose the wiring, never the hardware identity (that is NodeHardware).

item.title: Metrics Reference
item.description:
Every Prometheus metric the agent, the controller manager and the scheduler extender export, for dashboards and alerts. Simulator metrics are on Simulator Metrics; the metrics Joulie reads as input are on Input Telemetry and Actuation Interfaces.

Endpoints by component

Component Path Default address Override
Agent /metrics :8080 METRICS_ADDR
Controller manager /metrics :8081 METRICS_ADDR
Scheduler extender /metrics :9877 METRICS_ADDR

Agent metrics

Backend and selected cap

  • joulie_backend_mode{node,mode} (gauge)
    • mode: none|rapl|dvfs
    • active mode is 1, others 0
  • joulie_policy_cap_watts{node,policy} (gauge)
    • current selected policy cap in watts

RAPL power/energy

  • joulie_rapl_energy_uj{node,zone} (gauge)
    • latest raw RAPL energy counter in microjoules
  • joulie_rapl_estimated_power_watts{node,zone} (gauge)
    • per-zone estimated power from energy deltas
  • joulie_rapl_package_total_power_watts{node} (gauge)
    • sum of package-level estimated power

DVFS controller

  • joulie_dvfs_observed_power_watts{node} (gauge)
    • observed package power used by DVFS controller
  • joulie_dvfs_ema_power_watts{node} (gauge)
    • EMA-smoothed power used for decisions
  • joulie_dvfs_throttle_pct{node} (gauge)
    • current throttle percentage
  • joulie_dvfs_above_trip_count{node} (gauge)
    • consecutive above-threshold samples
  • joulie_dvfs_below_trip_count{node} (gauge)
    • consecutive below-threshold samples
  • joulie_dvfs_actions_total{node,action} (counter)
    • action: throttle_up|throttle_down

CPU frequency observability

  • joulie_dvfs_cpu_cur_freq_khz{node,cpu} (gauge)
    • current CPU/policy frequency in kHz
  • joulie_dvfs_cpu_max_freq_khz{node,cpu} (gauge)
    • enforced max frequency cap in kHz

Governors

Written by the agent’s governor control.

item.title: Upgrading
item.description:
What to check when you upgrade a Joulie installation from v0.2 to v0.3. Go through the list before running helm upgrade.

Before the upgrade

  • Apply the new CRDs. helm upgrade never updates CRDs, and the API server prunes every field the installed CRD does not know, such as the governor fields. Apply them first:

    kubectl apply -f charts/joulie/crds/

    Without a checkout, take them from the release chart: helm pull oci://registry.cern.ch/joulie/joulie --version <version> --untar --untardir /tmp/joulie-chart, then kubectl apply -f /tmp/joulie-chart/joulie/crds/.

item.title: Alerts and Runbooks
item.description:
The Joulie chart ships four alerting rules for the failures that leave a cluster looking managed while it is not: a cap that did not apply, an agent that cannot write its status, a stale digital twin, and nodes without measured power. Each has a runbook below that an operator, or an SRE agent, can follow step by step.

Installing the rules

The rules live in charts/joulie/alerts/joulie-alerts.yaml, in the Prometheus rule file format. With the Prometheus Operator, turn on the chart’s PrometheusRule:

item.title: CPU-Only Benchmark
item.description:
What Joulie’s policies do to energy per unit of work on a 40-node CPU cluster (KWOK). These results come from the Joulie simulator, a test bed for Joulie’s behaviour, not evidence of energy savings: its hardware behaviour is assumed or fitted, not measured on real nodes (Evidence-based evaluation).

Full report: experiments/01-cpu-only-benchmark/REPORT.md.

Setup

Nodes Count CPU Cores Eco cap
kwok-cpu-highcore 10 2 x AMD EPYC 9965 384 600 W
kwok-cpu-highfreq 10 2 x AMD EPYC 9375F 64 384 W
kwok-cpu-intensive 20 2 x AMD EPYC 9655 192 480 W
Item Value
Baselines A: simulator only, no power management; B: static partition (19 of 40 nodes performance); C: queue-aware
Power models SPECpower curves (9655, 9965); analytic model at sockets x TDP (9375F)
Eco cap 60 % of sockets x TDP
Load CPU utilization 0.55 to 0.58 under A
Runs 2026-10-28, 2 seeds and a repeat of the first run, measured at regime

Results

Baseline Energy per CPU unit against A, seed 1 / 2 Avg IT power against A CPU work done against A
B (static) +2.7 / +1.4 % +2.7 / +1.4 % +0.0 / -0.0 %
C (queue-aware) +2.1 / +2.5 % +1.8 / +2.5 % -0.3 / -0.0 %

A’s repeat differed by 0.24 % in energy per unit.

item.title: Governor Exploration
item.description:
Experiment 05 measures CPU and GPU governor presets as an energy dimension of their own, next to power caps, to choose the defaults Joulie ships. The results come from emulated nodes whose governor and clock physics rest on assumed parameters: they show the shape of each trade-off, not measured savings (#106).

Experiment folder: experiments/05-governor-exploration/. The presets are under Governor presets; governor control is off by default (GOVERNOR_CONTROL, GOVERNOR_WRITES, Configuration reference).

Questions

  • Q1: per CPU driver, which preset minimises energy to solution at each load, and at what cost in time?
  • Q2: per GPU family and workload kind, energy and time of each GPU preset, alone and with a 60 % cap?
  • Q3: with a receiver gate, how much do multi-GPU jobs gain from sustained?
  • Q4: at cluster level, do governors beat caps alone on energy without breaking the performance class?
  • Q5: which conclusions survive the assumed parameters?

A default passes on a profile when it lowers energy with a p95 slowdown of at most 5 % (performance class) and 20 % (eco class), in Tier A, in Tier B and at every value Q5 sweeps.

item.title: Heterogeneous GPU Cluster Benchmark
item.description:
What Joulie’s policies do to energy per unit of GPU work on a 41-node cluster of five GPU families (KWOK). These results come from the Joulie simulator, a test bed for Joulie’s behaviour, not evidence of energy savings: its hardware behaviour is assumed or fitted, not measured on real nodes (Evidence-based evaluation).

Full report: experiments/02-heterogeneous-benchmark/REPORT.md.

Setup

Nodes Count GPUs per node
kwok-h100-nvl 12 8 x NVIDIA H100 NVL
kwok-h100-sxm 6 4 x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3
kwok-l40s 7 4 x NVIDIA L40S
kwok-mi300x 2 8 x AMD Instinct MI300X
kwok-w7900 6 4 x AMD Radeon PRO W7900
CPU-only (EPYC 9965, 9375F, 9655) 8 none
Item Value
Baselines A: simulator only, no power management; B: static partition (31 of 41 nodes performance); C: queue-aware
Eco cap 70 % of each GPU’s maximum
Cap response exponent fitted per family to published data: H100 SXM 0.43, H100 NVL 0.50, MI300X 0.62, L40S 1.20, W7900 1.0 (no data)
Load GPU utilization 0.46 to 0.49 under A
Runs 2026-10-28, 2 seeds and a repeat of the first run, measured at regime

Results

Baseline GPU-node energy per GPU unit against A, seed 1 / 2 Avg IT power against A GPU work done against A Pending performance jobs (A: 0.7)
B (static) +0.1 / +4.6 % +3.6 / +3.0 % +3.6 / -1.4 % 3.5

item.title: Homogeneous H100 NVL Benchmark
item.description:
What Joulie’s policies do to power and energy per unit of GPU work on a 41-node cluster of H100 NVL nodes (KWOK). These results come from the Joulie simulator, a test bed for Joulie’s behaviour, not evidence of energy savings: its hardware behaviour is assumed or fitted, not measured on real nodes (Evidence-based evaluation).

Full report: experiments/03-homogeneous-h100-benchmark/REPORT.md.

Setup

Item Value
Nodes 33 H100 NVL nodes (8 GPUs each) and 8 CPU-only nodes
Baselines A: simulator only, no power management; B: static partition (27 of 41 nodes performance); C: queue-aware
Eco cap 280 W, 70 % of 400 W
Cap response computeGamma 0.50, the H100 PCIe’s published response, since the NVL has no published data (#106)
Load GPU utilization 0.55 to 0.58 under A
Runs 2026-10-28, 2 seeds and a repeat of the first run, measured at regime

item.title: Scoring Formula Validation
item.description:
Not a valid result. Its results do not stand and are not published. The experiment is to be redone on the scheduling logic extracted into an importable library (#122), as a behaviour scenario (#115).

An audit found that jobs that do not fit are dropped instead of queued, energy is divided by the placed jobs only, the arms are mislabelled, the selected formula never ran through the cooling model, and the formula was chosen and reported on the same 8 seeds. The scripts are Python models of the cluster, the cooling and the formula; they import no Joulie code and do not follow changes to the extender.
